pr_title: Don't wait for client methods to complete when stopping connection

issue_context.title: SignalR .NET client deadlocks when calling StopAsync inside On handler
comments: Might be related to https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/17584, not sure if StopAsync is different, we'll need to take a look.
Probably true, but also probably a different code path so we'll need to make a different fix.

It's the same code basically. Stop will wait for the receive loop to complete, but the receive loop waits on the `.On` handlers
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/6912dda560f52f761d9528dba786a7872ad1739f/src/SignalR/clients/csharp/Client.Core/src/HubConnection.cs#L1223
which is where Stop is being called from.

I can see two changes:
1. We don't wait for user methods and just `_ = StartProcessingInvocationMessages(...)`
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/6912dda560f52f761d9528dba786a7872ad1739f/src/SignalR/clients/csharp/Client.Core/src/HubConnection.cs#L1126
1. Put a time limit on how long we wait either at the end of the receive loop or in Stop

review_comments: Should we await this before allowing the HubConnection to be restarted? Is there any risk in letting `.On` handlers for the previous connection to still execute after the connection restarted?
Like reconnnects? Yes.. That makes sense

I don't have a great fix for stopping then starting in an On handler. I don't think we should break that.

The cleanest solution I can think of is to probably continue awaiting invocationMessageReceiveTask at the end of the ReceiveLoop, but then timing it out. If it times out, we could throw an exception indicating a possible deadlock that suggests dispatching the call to StopAsync() if it's made in an On handler.

That's a pretty big change though, and this is a definite improvement.
